Q: Find value in data from CSV read with Pandas A:

The reason your comparisons return False is that each cell in the ID column contains a single string, sometimes with two IDs separated by ", ".

For example, row 2 contains:

"15453278, 07320582"

So:

fcsv["ID"] == "07320582"

checks whether the entire cell value equals "07320582", which it does not.

You can search for an ID within the string using str.contains:

mask = fcsv["ID"].str.contains(r"\b07320582\b", na=False)
print(mask)

To get the row numbers:

rows = fcsv.index[mask]
print(rows.tolist())

Output:

[2]

If you want the first matching row:

row = fcsv.index[mask][0]
print(row)

Alternatively, a more robust approach is to split the IDs and test membership explicitly:

target = "07320582"

mask = fcsv["ID"].str.split(", ").apply(lambda ids: target in ids)
rows = fcsv.index[mask]
print(rows.tolist())

This avoids accidental partial matches

Q: IntelliJ/AndroidStudio: icon_banner_image.xml Not Found (Snap) A:

This issue typically occurs in newer versions of IntelliJ IDEA / Android Studio (especially when installed via Snap or the Ubuntu Software Store) because the Asset Studio wizard strictly looks for the default adaptive icon template files in the project's directory structure, but fails to generate or locate them due to sandbox path restrictions or template mismatches.

Since the Next button is disabled, you have to satisfy the wizard's strict file checks manually.

Solution : Create Dummy Placeholder Files (Quickest Fix)

The Asset Studio wizard is simply complaining that the default files do not exist in your resource directories. You can trick it by creating empty or basic XML drawable files with the exact names it wants.

  1. Navigate to your project's main resource directory: app/src/main/res/drawable/ (or res/mipmap/).

  2. Create three new files (if they don't already exist) named exactly:

    • ic_launcher_foreground.xml

    • ic_launcher_background.xml

    • ic_banner_image.xml

  3. Paste a minimal, valid XML vector code into each of them so the IDE doesn't throw a parsing error:

    <vector xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:width="100dp"
    android:height="100dp"
    android:viewportWidth="100"
    android:viewportHeight="100">
    <path android:fillColor="#FF000000" android:pathData="M0,0h100v100H0z"/>
</vector>

    Reopen the Asset Studio wizard. The error should vanish, and the "Next" button will be clickable. You can then safely overwrite these files using the wizard UI.

Q: PHP MYSQL Login Form, is there a better way to do it? A:

Only a few oversights I can add to the other two answers.

  • include et al. are something called "braceless language construct" (as opposed to brace-using language constructs) hence you are adding braces for no reason and your code actually looks like $str = ($name) . ($surname); - it works, but braces make zero sense here.
  • _once is an anachronism. It was a life saver some 20 years ago but has almost no use nowadays. All it does is sweeping problems with the code structure under the rug. You should drop it (and fix any issue that would appear, tough unlikely)
  • include doesn't stop the code execution in case the file is not found, but there is no reason not to do so. Therefore require it should be.
  • using empty() (a brace-using language construct by the way) with deliberately existing variables makes no sense and should be dropped in favor or checking variables themselves.
  • using empty() is considered a bad practice at all and should be dropped in favor of checking variables themselves against expected values using strict comparison
  • The ?? '' operator prevents warnings. That's a big one. Your job is not to "prevent warnings." But to prevent errors. Whereas warnings only indicate an error in your code and by no means should be prevented.
  • when a form field "was not sent at all" it's definitely an error, and there is no sense in handling such a form. Instead of "preventing warnings" you should add some validation that would respond with a 400 HTTP error and stop further processing in case some required field is not sent.

Q: Xcode doesn't show simulators A:

Go to Project → Targets → Build Settings → Excluded Architectures.

For both Debug and Release, the value should be Any iOS Simulator SDK only. Currently, arm64 (silicon) is added there. Please remove it, then close and reopen Xcode.
